content.title: About
content.content: Pork ears are edible parts of a pig's head that are typically prepared by boiling, roasting, or smoking. They have a dense, gelatinous texture and a distinctive meaty flavor with a slight crispness when fried.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork ears are used in traditional dishes around the world, such as Polish "ears in sour cream" and various Asian snacks.
In some cultures they are considered a delicacy because of their unique texture.
Ears are rich in collagen, which is why they are sometimes added to broths to improve gel strength.
They can be marinated, smoked, or dried, each method giving a different flavor profile.
In Russia pork ears are often served cold, thinly sliced as an appetizer.

items.title: Rich in collagen
items.content: Collagen in pork ears supports skin, joint, and connective‑tissue health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Pork ears provide a substantial amount of animal protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: They contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from pork ears helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ears contain vitamin B12 and other B‑vitamins important for nervous system function.

items.title: Pig meat allergy
items.content: People allergic to pork may react to pork ears.

items.title: High sodium in cured versions
items.content: Ears that are heavily salted or cured can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient cooking can lead to bacterial growth.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Pork ears contain a notable amount of fat, so they should be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pork ears can be boiled in broth, roasted in the oven, fried until crispy, or smoked. They are often sliced thin and served as a snack, added to salads, soups, or used as a garnish for main dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh ears refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. Frozen ears can be stored for up to 3 months. Before use, check that they have no off‑odor and no discoloration.
